correctness.rationale: The exact weighted variance identity and Cauchy-Schwarz establish sharp inequality var_m(g)≤sum(G_i/ell_i)(g_{i+1}-g_i)^2 with equality only g=c+d z; hence explicit path w0=ΛG_i/ell_i has simple Fiedler mode f and optimally attains Λ=B/V. Rayleigh on f gives λ2≤[B-(q-S²)t]/V, yielding q>threshold path uniqueness and critical upper bound. At q<S² a feasible infinitesimal t increases the simple eigenvalue by (S²-q)/V, so every optimum uses t>0. At equality eigenvector equations force w_i(t)=w_i0-tS/ell_i; on mean-zero vectors orthogonal to f the precise form A-tR stays PSD iff t≤min_g A(g)/R(g), with A,R strictly positive by equality conditions. Independent random heterogeneous cases verified budgets, eigenpairs and finite critical face; no infinite theorem inferred from numerics.

final_claim: For continuous-time reversible cycle generator with arbitrary positive vertex masses and independently priced path conductances p_i, optional closing-edge price q and budget B, the sharp screening price is q_c=(sum sqrt(p_i))^2 irrespective of masses. At q>q_c the unique optimizer is an explicit weighted path; below it every optimizer uses positive closing edge; at q=q_c the complete optimizer set is the affine interval whose endpoint is min(edge-nonnegativity cutoff, generalized spectral cutoff on the mass-orthogonal complement).
limitations: Only n>=3 single closing edge, positive masses/costs and continuous-time generalized spectral gap, no arbitrary chords, discrete-time constraints or explicit below-threshold design.
